purpose: Resolve the selected return-frequency concept into one exact finite no-value mechanism and challenge it against terminal and prospective families before any Campaign033 source partition, candidate value, comparison value, daily price, or forward return is opened.

selected_mechanism.name: intraday_return_spectral_entropy_59f
selected_mechanism.formula: -sum(p_k * log(p_k)) / log(59) for k=1..59, where p_k is pooled morning-plus-afternoon demeaned signed-return DFT power at positive frequency k divided by total pooled positive-frequency power
selected_mechanism.economic_hypothesis: A higher value means return energy is distributed broadly across intraday frequencies instead of being dominated by a small periodic or slowly varying structure, representing less mechanically concentrated price formation that may carry resilience from the next open through the third close.
selected_mechanism.selected_bar_grid: exactly 240 one-minute closes at 09:31-11:30 and 13:01-15:00 after frozen timestamp normalization; standalone 09:30 is excluded and no return crosses lunch
selected_mechanism.return_rule: Form 119 natural-log close returns separately inside each 120-close half. Retain signed and exact-zero returns and subtract each half's arithmetic mean from its own 119-vector.
selected_mechanism.dft_rule: For each demeaned 119-vector compute the unnormalized length-119 discrete Fourier transform with exponent -2*pi*i*j*k/119. Retain exactly positive-frequency bins k=1 through 59; do not use k=0 or duplicate negative-frequency bins.
selected_mechanism.power_pooling_rule: For each k, add squared complex magnitudes from the morning and afternoon coefficients. Pool power before entropy; do not average two half-session entropies and do not join returns across lunch.
selected_mechanism.entropy_rule: Divide each of the 59 pooled powers by their strictly positive total. Terms with exact p_k=0 contribute zero. Use natural logarithms and divide Shannon entropy by log(59).
selected_mechanism.bar_rule: All 240 selected closes must be finite and strictly positive before log returns are formed.
selected_mechanism.endpoint_rule: Only values within 1e-12 of 0 or 1 may be canonicalized to the exact endpoint; no statistical clipping is allowed.
selected_mechanism.missing_rule: Any invalid or nonpositive close, nonfinite return, nonfinite DFT power, nonpositive total positive-frequency power, nonfinite score, or score outside [0,1] after endpoint canonicalization makes the stock-day missing.

overlap_challenges.reason: Return-variance entropy is a time-domain allocation statistic over individual squared returns and is invariant to permutation. Campaign033 is a frequency-domain allocation statistic; reordering the same signed returns can change every nonzero-frequency power while leaving time-domain variance entropy unchanged.

Those factors use adjacent products or lag-one absolute-return dependence. Campaign033 uses signed returns and the complete 59-bin power distribution, contains no selected lag or adjacent-product ratio, and discards phase only after the full-half DFT.

Sign-run mechanisms count selected discrete sign transitions and may discard magnitude. Campaign033 retains every signed magnitude, applies no sign threshold, and measures continuous frequency power rather than run counts.

Campaign027 correlates morning and afternoon signed return vectors at matching ordinal positions and depends on cross-half phase alignment. Campaign033 sums their powers at matching frequencies and is invariant to each half's cyclic phase; it never pairs morning return j with afternoon return j.

Volatility resolution compares morning and afternoon total squared-return mass, while time-allocation factors emphasize when activity occurs. Campaign033 pools the halves equally at each frequency and depends on normalized frequency shape, not morning-versus-afternoon level or clock-time mass.

Demeaning and excluding k=0 removes the half-session mean-return component. Net displacement, late return, and terminal location can change without uniquely determining the 59-bin normalized spectrum.

Candidate49 measures repeated crossings around causal cumulative VWAP using close, volume, and amount. Campaign033 reads close only, contains no transaction anchor or crossing count, and remains historical-research-only.
Campaign020 and Campaign032 use corporate disclosure dates and no price path. Campaign033 uses only the completed signal-session intraday close path and no quarterly field.
Campaign033 contains one raw close-path frequency statistic and no terminal factor value, transform, filter, model, or combination.
